newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy calls U.S. strike in Iraq "inevitable".
newsitem.headline: Italy calls U.S. strike in Iraq "inevitable".

text.p: Italy on Tuesday called the U.S. cruise missile strikes on targets in Iraq an "inevitable response" to Baghdad's military attacks on Kurds but stopped short of expressing outright support for the operation.

A Foreign Ministry statement said Italy was following developments in Iraqi Kurdistan with "attention and concern" and was in close contact with its partners on ways of stopping the situation from escalating.
It appealed to all sides to "abstain from actions and behaviour which could raise tension further and from exploiting issues concerning the Kurdish populations to do this".
Earlier on Tuesday the U.S. military fired 27 long-range cruise missiles against air defence and communications targets in southern Iraq.
"This morning's American action is an inevitable response to Iraq's attack in Kurdistan and to the failure by Baghdad to implement United Nations resolutions," the statement said.
"This could not but provoke sanctionary measures."
The statement said Italy, a NATO ally of Washington, had been informed in advance of the U.S. strikes.
Britain and Germany have voiced strong support for the raid while France and Spain have expressed reservations. The Italian statement gave no indication whether Rome supported the action.
In Baghdad, Iraqi television reported that Iraq's defiant President Saddam Hussein said damage from the strike was minimal and that many missiles were shot down.
He urged Iraqi troops to resist and said his country would no longer recognise "no-fly zones" policed by allied warplanes over northern and southern Iraq.
